lines.text: Let's put it all together, with every idea switched on.
One. Far away, use the map. Near the target, measure the target's own tag.
Two. Place every photo where the robot was when it was taken, in the smooth wheel world.
Three. Blend photos into a smart average that trusts close photos, and ignores jumps and unsure photos.
Four. Fix each camera once, because a crooked camera is wrong the same way every time.
Check yourself. Question one: why does the tag live in the wheel world? Pause and think.
The wheel pose never jumps, so the tag stays still. And the goal is measured from the robot each loop, so jumps cancel.
Question two: the robot drives two meters per second, and a photo is zero point zero five seconds old. Without the rewind, how far off?
Speed times age: two times zero point zero five. Ten centimeters.
Question three: our variance equals the photo's noise. What's the gain, and how far does the guess move?
The gain is one half, so the guess moves halfway to the photo.
Question four: a camera is turned two degrees, and the tag is one and a half meters away. How far sideways does it look?
One and a half times the tangent of two degrees. About five centimeters.
Question five: why can't averaging more photos fix that error?
Every photo is off the same way. The average of the same mistake is the same mistake. Calibrate instead.
